not_available: PyPI exposes neither maintainers nor per-version publishers: publisher history is unavailable for PyPI dependencies
crates.io exposes the publisher of each version but not the owner set at the time: maintainer changes are npm only
registry back-link (does the repository claim the package?) is not checked; correspondence means the pointers agree
registry events are read from metadata only: dependency tarballs are never downloaded or inspected
structural parsing does not evaluate Starlark, Nix or Buck macros
only fetched files are read (workflows, manifests, scripts, build files, a source sample): a host in an unread file is unknown, not absent
a hostname in a file means the file refers to it; no connection is observed and no host is resolved or contacted
external_domain_* events need a revision comparison (diff): one analysis has no introduction time
maintainer_change / ownership_change: current-state only; per-version maintainers exist for npm dependencies
dependency domains: dependency tarballs are never fetched, so they are not observed
dependency behavior/trust-boundary deltas require two inspected artifacts with verified digests

findings.title: Download-and-execute chain observed in Makefile
findings.summary: Directly observed path: remote download -> piped directly into a shell/interpreter (line 5). Context: build. This describes a capability; the purpose of the download is undetermined.
findings.remediation: Verify what is downloaded: pin a version and check a checksum or signature before executing, or vendor the artifact.

findings.title: Download-and-execute chain observed in completions.go
findings.summary: Directly observed path: remote download -> piped directly into a shell/interpreter (line 910). Context: runtime. This describes a capability; the purpose of the download is undetermined.
findings.remediation: Verify what is downloaded: pin a version and check a checksum or signature before executing, or vendor the artifact.

findings.title: make hook "Makefile" runs code at build time
findings.summary: Stage SOURCE_BUILD, trigger USER_INVOKED, environment HOST. Trigger: make (default target). Observed capabilities: FILESYSTEM_DELETE, REMOTE_DOWNLOAD.
findings.remediation: Review the hook and the files it runs before installing; consider installing with lifecycle scripts disabled (for npm: --ignore-scripts) where the package allows it.

findings.title: Persistence capability observed (shell_profile_modification)
findings.summary: Files in the scanned sample contain constructs that can make software start again after login or reboot. Installers, agents and servers legitimately do this; intent is undetermined.
findings.remediation: Confirm that the persistence is documented, expected for this kind of software, and removable.

regulatory.disclaimer: repo-radar performs technical readiness and applicability analysis from repository evidence. It does not provide legal advice and does not determine legal compliance or non-compliance. Repository contents alone may be insufficient to decide whether a regulation applies: deployment context, the role of the organization, jurisdiction and the commercial distribution context all matter. An indicator that is "not observed" means no evidence was found in the analyzed repository revision, not that a control is absent.

indicators.title: A security policy / vulnerability disclosure channel is published
indicators.reference: CRA Annex I Part II (vulnerability handling): coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy (indicative)
indicators.limitations: A file existing says nothing about whether the process is operated; an organization-level policy in another repository is only partly visible.

indicators.title: A software bill of materials is committed and parsable
indicators.reference: CRA Annex I Part II (identify and document components, incl. an SBOM) (indicative)
indicators.limitations: SBOMs published only as release assets are not fetched; an SBOM can be present and inaccurate (see the SBOM comparison findings).

indicators.title: Dependencies are inventoried with exact versions
indicators.reference: CRA Annex I Part II (identify and document vulnerabilities and components) (indicative)
indicators.limitations: Libraries commonly publish ranges on purpose; the ratio covers direct registry dependencies only.

indicators.title: Dependency vulnerabilities are checked and updates are automated
indicators.reference: CRA Annex I Part II (address and remediate vulnerabilities; regular testing) (indicative)
indicators.limitations: Reflects tooling present in the repository, not how findings are triaged or fixed.

indicators.title: Releases are published and recent
indicators.reference: CRA Annex I Part II (security updates made available) (indicative)
indicators.limitations: Projects that publish only to a registry or via tags can look unreleased here.

indicators.title: Tests, static analysis and branch protection are in place
indicators.reference: CRA Annex I Part I (security-by-design practices) (indicative)
indicators.limitations: Branch protection is only visible with a suitable token; heuristics detect tests and SAST by name.

indicators.title: Release provenance or signatures are published
indicators.reference: CRA Annex I Part II (integrity of updates) (indicative)
indicators.limitations: Provenance is often published to the package registry instead, where this analysis does not look.

indicators.title: Support and security-update period information is documented
indicators.limitations: Support terms are frequently stated in a README or on a website, which this check does not read.
